styles.base: Korean traditional minhwa folk painting in ink-wash damchae style: confident black ink brush outlines, soft muted watercolor washes of indigo, ochre, persimmon red and pine green on aged hanji paper texture. Bright, clear, high contrast, faces large and readable. Joseon dynasty. No text, no letters anywhere.
styles.sil: Korean minhwa ink-wash painting on hanji paper mixed with bold acrylic painting in the style of a sunset landscape: sky of layered flat gray and silver clouds with ribbons of gold, orange and red glowing between them, figures and trees as solid black silhouettes, blue-violet shadows. Joseon dynasty. No text, no letters anywhere.
styles.web: Korean traditional minhwa folk painting in ink-wash damchae style, matching the style of the reference image: confident black ink brush outlines, soft muted watercolor washes of indigo, ochre, persimmon red and pine green on aged cream hanji paper. Bright and clear, faces large and readable. No text, no letters anywhere.

characters.YEONGDAL: a man in his forties whose head is bare with only a cloth band tied round his topknot, there is never a hat on his head, plain undyed hemp jacket and gray trousers
characters.JO: a man in his late thirties with a thin mustache, a fine pale silk durumagi and a wide black gat hat that sits loosely on his head
characters.MAGISTRATE: the county magistrate, a dignified man with a short beard in a crimson official robe and black official hat

scenes.S01: A close view filling the frame: ten black Korean gat hats lying empty on a straw mat on bare earth, seen from directly above, their wide brims overlapping. The hats are empty objects on the ground. There are no people, no heads, no faces anywhere in the picture.
scenes.S02: A poor commoner in a plain undyed hemp jacket, his head bare with only a cloth band and no hat, standing in a county office courtyard and holding one black gat hat upside down above his head with both hands. A magistrate in a crimson robe stands to the side watching him. Daylight.
scenes.S05: Only one person in the picture: YEONGDAL sitting cross legged on the floor of a small workshop, bare headed with his hair in a topknot, weaving fine black horsehair on a small round wooden form held in his lap, bundles of horsehair beside him. Nobody else, warm daylight through the paper door.
scenes.S06: A close view filling the frame: two weathered hands splitting a thin bamboo strip with a small knife and weaving the fine strips into the flat wide brim of a gat hat on a low work board. Only hands and the work, no face. Nothing written.
scenes.S07: Exactly two people at a workshop door: YEONGDAL, bare headed with a topknot, holding out a finished black gat hat with both hands, and a man in a silk durumagi and a black gat receiving it. Daylight. Nobody else.
scenes.S08: A close view filling the frame: one black gat hat lying upside down on a low wooden work board, seen from above looking down into its crown, and two bare hands weaving fine horsehair inside it. The hat is an object on the table, nobody is wearing it, no head and no face in the picture.
scenes.S09: [SIL] Sunset over a village road, a line of men in wide brimmed gat hats walking as black silhouettes, layered gray and silver clouds with ribbons of gold behind them.
scenes.S10: YEONGDAL squatting behind a straw mat in a market street with five black gat hats laid out on it, two customers in hemp clothes leaning down to look. He is bare headed with a head cloth. Daylight, nothing written.
scenes.S11: Exactly two people inside a small workshop: YEONGDAL kneeling and measuring the head of an old man with a white beard using a paper strip, the old man sitting straight with his eyes closed. Nobody else, daylight.
scenes.S12: Only one person in the picture: JO, a man in his late thirties in a fine pale silk durumagi and a black gat hat, walking into a village street with a confident face, a small bundle in one hand. Nobody else, daylight.
scenes.S13: Six men sitting on the floor of a Korean room around a low table, one of them in a fine silk coat talking with a raised hand, the others leaning in and listening eagerly. Daylight through the paper door, nothing written.
scenes.S14: Four men in a Korean room handing small cloth money pouches across a low table to a man in a fine silk coat who accepts them with both hands and a smile. Daylight, nothing written.
scenes.S15: Exactly two people in a market street: JO in a silk coat and black gat walking past, and YEONGDAL standing aside with his head turned, staring at the gat hat. Daylight, stalls behind.
scenes.S16: A close view filling the frame: YEONGDAL looking up with narrowed eyes and a frozen face, his head bare with only a cloth band round his topknot and no hat on his head, softly blurred market street behind him. Nobody else.
scenes.S17: Only one person in the picture: JO walking in a street and reaching up with one hand to push his black gat hat back into place, the hat sitting loosely and tipped forward on his head. Nobody else, daylight.
scenes.S19: Exactly two people in a market street: YEONGDAL leaning in and asking something with a serious face, and an old market woman answering with her hand raised. Daylight, stalls behind. Nobody else.
scenes.S20: Only one person in the picture: YEONGDAL walking through a county office gate with a determined face, bare headed with a head cloth, his hands empty. Daylight, tiled wall. Nobody else.
scenes.S21: Exactly two people in a county office courtyard: a county clerk in a dark navy coat standing with folded arms and a scornful face, and YEONGDAL standing before him bare headed. Daylight. Nobody else.
scenes.S22: Exactly three people at a county office gate: two servants in dark clothes pushing YEONGDAL out, and a clerk watching from behind. Daylight.
scenes.S24: Only one person in the picture: YEONGDAL walking up a village lane carrying a wooden A frame on his back stacked with ten black gat hats tied together, his face set. Daylight, low walls. Nobody else.
scenes.S25: YEONGDAL kneeling on the bare ground of a county office courtyard laying out ten black gat hats in two rows on a straw mat, a magistrate in a crimson robe watching from the stone step and a crowd standing behind. Daylight.
scenes.S26: YEONGDAL holding one black gat hat upside down with both hands showing the inside of its crown, and four men in gat hats leaning in close to look inside it with serious faces. Ten more hats lie on a straw mat on the ground. Daylight courtyard.
scenes.S27: Exactly two people in a courtyard: a county clerk in a dark navy coat lifting the black gat hat off the head of JO, who stands stiffly with his bare topknot showing and a pale face. A crowd watches behind. Daylight.
scenes.S28: A close view: YEONGDAL holding up two black gat hats upside down side by side at chest height, showing both insides, his face calm. Blurred courtyard crowd behind. Nothing written.
scenes.S29: Only one person in the picture: JO standing stiffly in a courtyard without his hat, his topknot bare, his face pale and his hands trembling at his sides. Daylight, nobody else.
scenes.S30: Exactly two people in the front of a crowd: an old servant in worn hemp clothes pointing at JO with a shaking hand, and JO standing hatless with his head down. Daylight courtyard, crowd behind.
scenes.S32: Exactly two people leading a bound man away in a courtyard: two constables in dark clothes holding the arms of JO, who is hatless with his head down and his arms tied with rope. Villagers watching from the side. Daylight.
scenes.S33: Exactly two people in a county office courtyard: a magistrate in a crimson official robe speaking with a kind face from the stone step, and YEONGDAL standing below bare headed with his hands folded. Daylight, nobody else.
scenes.S34: A close view filling the frame: YEONGDAL speaking with a calm steady face, his head bare with only a cloth band round his topknot and no hat on his head, softly blurred courtyard behind. Nobody else.
scenes.S35: A close view filling the frame: one black gat hat lying upside down on a low table, seen from above looking down into its crown, and two hands pressing a tiny stamp inside it. The hat is an object on the table, nobody wears it, no head and no face, no readable letters.
scenes.S36: Three men in gat hats crouching around a straw mat of black gat hats in a market street, each turning one hat upside down to look inside it, a seller squatting behind the mat. Daylight, nothing written.
scenes.S37: [SIL] Sunset over a village road, a line of men in wide brimmed gat hats walking as black silhouettes, and one bare headed man with a head cloth standing to the side watching them, layered silver clouds and a band of gold light.
